title: Tapper, from Augustine
source_text: XLIX. Eadem de fidelium in hac vita imperfectione circa legem implendam, ex Augustino quoque, docet Ruardus Tapperus Professor Lovaniensis, in defensione articuli secundi pag. 76. Ubi affirmat, post sanctum illum Doctorem, esse quidem hic sanitatem, novitatem & justitiam, sed non plenam, nec perfectam, nisi modo quodam: sicut non hic est plena dilectio. Et legem, cujus plenitudo dilectio est, tunc demum ita implendam ut nihil omnino desit, quum dilectio Dei perfecta erit. Dei vero dilectionem non futuram esse perfectam antequam Deum videamus.
pass_a_gloss: XLIX. The same things concerning the imperfection of the faithful in this life as regards fulfilling the law, from Augustine also, does Ruard Tapper Professor at Louvain teach, in the defence of the second article page 76. Where he affirms, after that holy Doctor, that there is indeed here health, newness & righteousness, but not full, nor perfect, except in a certain manner: as here there is not full love. And that the law, whose fullness is love, is then at last to be so fulfilled that nothing at all is lacking, when the love of God will be perfect. But that the love of God will not be perfect before we see God.
pass_b_english: Thesis XLIX. Ruard Tapper, professor at Louvain, teaches the same about the imperfection of believers in this life with respect to fulfilling the law, drawing on Augustine as well, in his defence of the second article, page 76.

Following that holy doctor, he says that health, newness and righteousness do exist here, but not in full and not perfectly, except in a certain way, just as love is not full here. The law, whose fulfilment is love, will be fulfilled so completely that nothing at all is missing only when love for God is perfect; and love for God will not be perfect until we see God.

choices.english: a righteousness worthy of the name
choices.why: Stapleton's claim that the imperfect righteousness of this life is still true righteousness.
